scopeBoundary: Reviewed source logic, wording and analytically projected layout only. No code execution, Unity, GPU, UI or render verification was performed. Initial line numbers refer to the inspected pre-fix source; the root subsequently authorized fixes in the grid class and sampling helper only.
overall: The script retains all nine mapped source sections in order. The initial eight mode routes cover the broad narrative, but four demonstrations do not yet show the mechanism promised by their labels: one-shot attack, attack timing, pose-document workflow and joint limit. These are substantive explanation issues rather than merely visual polish.

modes.evidence: One actor samples Walk_A at0.30s; the other samples the same clip at t. This supports pose versus movement.
limitations: It does not demonstrate two interpretations of a vague walking instruction. The narration may explain that in general, but do not claim this particular A/B proves personality differences.
A sampled clip pose is not a measured centre of mass or weight distribution.

modes.evidence: Three highlighted rows choose Idle_A, Walk_A and FightM_Punch_A. However the common sampler repeats every clip, including the row labelled one shot.

The12/60=0.2s equation is correct and labelled illustrative, but the marker uses a1-second clock while the arm animation repeats at its own clip length. The global bottom playhead uses total cut duration.
Two identical static FightM_Punch_A samples at0.3s are shown; one uses a dark lit material. No pose→capture→isolate→annotate sequence or object-attached notes is implemented.

Held punch pose at0.05s beside a moving punch supports a reference/result comparison. It is not a revised version A/B and does not by itself cover paired interaction, weapon, dodge, idle and expressive gesture roles.
LookingAround is applied to two owned character variants. This can show a recurring gesture transferred between bodies if rigs and visible identity match.
limitations: It is a same-clip transfer demonstration, not evidence of a commercial game's reference process.
A frozen reference thumbnail would more directly illustrate keeping screenshots as a specification, but the script already states that method.
The nonhumanoid Goose role must be supplied by independently verified footage in the edit.

modes.evidence: The same static FightM_Pose receives fixed local-Z offsets of-55° and-15°. No requested angle, clamp or varying reachable boundary is implemented.
Routes to exactly the same build and apply logic as motion-brief. Shows movement around a held pose, but no actual revised motion, review note or shared feedback process.

findings.title: The one-shot row actually loops
findings.issue: ApplyPose always uses Mathf.Repeat(seconds,clip.length). Once the attack row is selected, its attack loops even though the lesson explicitly contrasts one-shot and repeated motions. Passing global t also starts the new row at an arbitrary clip phase.
findings.recommendedFix: Use row-local time; keep idle/walk looping, sample attack once and clamp at the actual clip duration. Preserve the existing default looping sampler for other modes.
findings.acceptance: After the attack row becomes active, one complete attack begins at clip time0, reaches its final pose and stays there for the remainder of that row. Loop rows visibly reconnect to the beginning.

findings.title: The timing interval and arm animation use different clocks
findings.issue: The red state uses t modulo1, the attack uses t modulo actual clip.length, and the bottom cursor uses total capture length. Unless durations happen to match, the advertised attack interval drifts relative to the arm. There are no active colliders/events, so this is not a measured hitbox interval.
findings.recommendedFix: Declare a1-second own illustrative timeline. Drive both the sampled arm action and its cursor/12-frame selected range from that clock. Label it as a chosen design example, not detected attack frames or measured commercial-game data.
findings.acceptance: At60fps the highlighted range contains frames12 through23, exactly12 samples/0.2s; its start/end and sampled action share a documented mapping. A runtime reviewer confirms the intended arm segment and the loop boundary.

findings.title: Two arm offsets do not demonstrate a joint limit
findings.issue: Both figures are held at a static base pose. Applying different constants shows two poses, without showing that both request the same target and one cannot reach it. The code comment acknowledges an artificial limit, but the viewer cannot see the limiting operation.
findings.recommendedFix: Animate one shared requested angle, apply it unrestricted on one side and clamp the same request at an explicitly illustrative30° upper bound on the other. Show target versus allowed range. Define angles as extra rotation relative to this pose rather than a universal anatomical/asset limit; avoid accumulating offsets across frames.
findings.acceptance: Both arms follow the same request below30°; above30° only the unrestricted arm continues. The visual identifies the intentional limit and retains the lesson that reference intent may require adaptation. No claim of measured natural joint limits or validated skin/prop collision unless separately shown.

findings.title: The promised pose-document workflow is absent
findings.issue: Narration lists pose, camera/capture, isolation/contrast and short intention notes. Initial code displays only two simultaneous frozen characters, so the central production-document method is replaced by a generic pose comparison.
findings.recommendedFix: Stage the reference→isolated silhouette→annotated specification progression. Keep the exact same pose and framing to show continuity. Add short leader lines to the relevant arm/feet, and distinguish a digital workflow illustration from a real photograph/export operation.
findings.acceptance: A viewer can identify the input pose, what was removed/simplified, and the final reusable instruction at the corresponding speech. Do not label a file as saved/captured unless an actual file was created.

findings.title: The silhouette uses lighting and the note does not point to a target
findings.issue: Tint assigns a lit URP material, so lights can vary the intended silhouette tone. The general note about arm direction and feet is not connected to those features. Its y350 block is near the top of the projected figure and may cover raised parts.
findings.recommendedFix: Use a flat unlit mask treatment for the silhouette illustration, with a clear isolated background and leader lines. Place notes outside the figure, not on the head/arm region.
findings.acceptance: The silhouette remains a uniform readable shape, labels point to the correct body part, and no note covers the intended pose at1080p/mobile.

findings.title: Attack labels occupy the projected actor region; picture-kind chip is duplicated
findings.issue: For the centred timing actor, orthographicSize3.2 at cameraY1.8 places a grounded2.7-unit body approximately at screenY388–840. The equation centred at y396 spans356–436 across that actor, and the bottom label at y818 spansabout786–851 across its feet. This is an analytic overlap risk, not a claimed screenshot observation. Additionally the stage renders '우리 Unity 시연' near1710,67 while the base comment reserves the final compositor's picture-kind chip at1740,73.
findings.recommendedFix: Separate the timing diagram/text from the actor, and use one clock-specific playhead. Reserve the existing compositor chip area instead of drawing a second picture-kind label there.
findings.acceptance: Root inspects real rendered output with final captions/chip at1920×1080 and375px width. Head, arm and feet are unobscured during the meaningful action.

findings.title: Comparison labels overstate what the sampled punch establishes
findings.issue: Labels describe centre/weight transfer even while the right clip proceeds through all phases. There is no COM/weight calculation, and motion-brief and pose-connection are identical. A static pose versus time-varying copy does not demonstrate a reviewed improvement.
findings.recommendedFix: Use descriptive pose/motion labels unless actual sampled frames substantiate the specific body-position claim. In the final edit, use a real changed parameter/version or explicit review note when explaining iteration, rather than presenting the same clip as improved.
findings.acceptance: No measured centre-of-mass/quality claim is implied. The final iteration passage visibly shows the identified change or a concrete review note.

findings.title: Some required example roles are only narrated, not provided by these modes
findings.issue: The script preserves paired contact, weapon, dodge, idle and gesture roles and the review/team-learning conclusion. The inspected Unity modes only provide punch/walk/look-around; they do not themselves demonstrate paired body contact, prop trajectory, dodge, revised result or shared feedback. This is an assembly requirement, not proof that the final edit omits these roles, because independent footage/annotations can supply them.
findings.recommendedFix: Bind each retained role to its actual independent game shot or own scene. Do not use eight mode names as evidence that all source roles are visually complete.
findings.acceptance: Final scene/cut mapping shows observed before/action/result for each retained role, including the shared review note at the conclusion.

positiveFindings: The same licensed character/camera and grid support controlled comparisons.
The12/60=0.2s calculation is correct and already introduced as a chosen example.
All source claims/order remain in the narration; noninstructional creator biography is omitted without losing the teaching structure.
Self-authored Unity is explicitly separated from commercial gameplay in the project plan.
The sampler restores model root transforms; pose diagnostics record actual own baked vertices/bones rather than invented game measurements.
remainingRuntimeChecks: Selected Arm.L hierarchy and local-Z direction actually raise the intended arm without unsuitable deformation.
Grounding by the lowest skinned vertex does not introduce visible vertical bob or use a hanging accessory as the floor contact.
The selected fixed punch times and action timing map correspond to readable poses in the actual asset.
The silhouette, leader lines and all labels remain readable with final fixed captions and picture-kind chip.
Final narration/scene mapping preserves the independent paired interaction, weapon and nonhumanoid evidence, plus visible iterative feedback.

implemented: The shared sampling helper now distinguishes looping, one-shot seconds and normalized illustrative sampling. Existing Pose callers retain looping behavior; Once clamps against the loaded clip.length.
motion-list uses row-local time, Loop for idle/walk and Once for the attack. The attack freezes after the actual clip duration instead of repeating.

attack-timing places its diagram left and actor right, using one explicit1-second clock for normalized action sampling, cursor and the selected[12/60,24/60) interval. It is labelled a chosen design example rather than measured collision; no colliders or hit detection were added.

pose-document now progresses through pose/capture illustration, isolated flat-unlit silhouette on a sheet, and short hand/foot intention notes with bone-anchored leader lines. The scene remains an illustrative digital workflow; it does not claim a screenshot/photo file was saved.

joint-limit now drives both copies from the same requested0–55-degree extra local-Z rotation; one copy clamps at30degrees. Static labels identify example angles and an added-rotation cap. Moving bars visualize the shared request and constrained result. Absolute base-relative rotations prevent offset accumulation.

Removed the duplicate picture-kind chip so the compositor owns its reserved corner. Renamed the global cursor to explanation progress and replaced unmeasured centre/weight-transfer labels with reference-pose/connecting-motion labels.
remediation.knownStringsConstraint: All numerical/text labels are fixed literals prepared by the existing rasterizer; only shapes, visibility and sampled poses animate. No new dynamic numeric string path or rasterizer change was introduced.

boneNameEvidence.kind: read-only existing diagnostic inspection, not a new runtime test
boneNameEvidence.limit: Presence is confirmed in the selected hero's earlier pose diagnostic. The direction and quality of the new local-Z demonstration still require the root's new sample review.
